answer: Standing is a thread that only holds when strangers pull it from both ends: each epoch’s work must be reproducible — strangers must independently redo it and get the same result — and a ferrous thread only holds when it is pulled from both ends, while an inlet only lets in work that strangers can redo. A farm of a thousand fakes cannot reproduce each other’s work: their work is not real, so no stranger can redo it and get the same result — and one epoch of unreproducible work adds nothing.
